about: Every message Aaron typed or dictated in this session on Terra (the PC), copied verbatim from its log on 25 September 2026. Only his words. Taken from both places the log keeps them - the queued record of every message he sends and the plain user records - each message kept once at its earliest time. Messages he sent while Claude was still working sit in time order with the rest and are not marked apart, because a queued record alone does not show that. System text, tool output, skill instructions, task notifications, cross-session messages, compaction summaries and anything the studio wrote are excluded, as are the helper agents' logs beside this one.
title: Hosting NationStates on GitHub

messages.text: I created a github account. Is it possible to upload nationstates to my github account (free) and use that as a place for people to test nationstates?
Is there anything in the readme or anything else in the documentation that would leak my IP Address or any personal information

Is there a better way to do this where when I want to push this out we would compile everything into a folder that only has the files needed to run the game instead of everything including the claude.md files and other things?
Can you push to it if I keep it private to start with
ok and how would I play it in browser
I have never used github before so how do I set it up on github for others
Can you do one final read through of what was pushed to github that there are no security vulnerabilies I am putting out to the world
Ok it is public what is next

Ok it is playing in git hub right now. Awesome!

Question about how this is coded with trade deals. Do they only last one turn?

Ok, that is something that needs to be changed, but not right now. As I am play testing it I am finding that there are a lot of cool mechanics but they aren't working together correctly or they aren't working in the right way. This as an example - would work better as a set time because if I am trading with a country and they get attacked and they are where I get food then I will defend them. The other thing is that the point of the rail network toll was that you could create long term trading with other people, with the goal being that if I am Utah and Idaho gets invaded by Washington then I lose my corridor to Canada and will either need to pay a higher toll or fight with Idaho. 

So right there is one thing (trading) but it intersects with economy, diplomacy, and military. 

So the question isn't how to fix them but how do I go about figuring out how to fix things and in what order. 

One thought is we create a branch that is a very very scaled back version of the game (just economy, diplomacy, military) and figure out those foundational things first and then add back in the other things and see how they interact and go from there. 

The other thing is just go one thing at a time.

For gave development which isthe best?
